FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Farm 
Implements and Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved by the Fbod and Agriculture Division 
Council. 

Dibble iron is a tool used for planting naked rooted plants in the forest as well as for field sowing. In order to 
produce quality dibble iron this standard has been prepared. 

In preparation of this standard assistance has been derived from Forest Research Institute, Dehra Dun. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)*. The number of significant places retained in 
the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



IS 14524 : 1998 



Indian Standard 



FORESTRY TOOLS — DIBBLE IRON 
SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard specifies the materials, dimensions and 
other requirements of the dibble iron used for planting 
naked rooted plants in the forest as well as for field 
sowing. 

2 REFERENCES 

The Indian Standards as given below contain 
provisions which through reference in this text, 
constitute provision of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most recent 
editions of the standards indicated: 



IS No. 
2062 : 1992 

2102 (Parti): 
1993 



2507 : 1975 
3601 : 1984 



Title 

Steel for general structural purposes 
(fourth revision) 

General tolerances: Part 1 
Tolerances for linear and angular 
dimensions without individual 
tolerance indications (third 
revision) 

Cold-rolled steel strips for springs 
(first revision) 

Steel tubes for mechanical and 
general engineering purposes (first 
revision) 

3 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

The dimensions of the dibble iron shall be as given in 
Fig. 1 . The tolerances on dimensions shall be of coarse 
class specified in IS 2102 (Part 1). 

4 MATERIAL 

The various components of the dibble iron shall be 
made from materials as given below: 
Component Materials 

Handle Steel tube (see IS 3601) 

Dibble point High carbon steel (conforming 

to grade 80 C 6 of IS 2507) 
Foot push support Mild steel (see IS 2062) 
and others 



5 OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 Dibble iron shall be provided with three different 
types of dibble points depending upon the size of the 
plant to be planted or the size of the seed to be sown. 

5 1.1 The removal and fitment of dibble point to the 
handle shall be easy and convenient. The dibble point 
shall not become loose during operation. 

5.2 The dibble points shall be sharpened to required 
size. 

53 The weight of the tool shall not exceed 2.75 
kilograms. 

5.4 The height of the tool shall be adjustable to 
increase or decrease depending upon the convenience 
of the worker subject to a maximum height of 1 100 
millimetres. 

6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

6.1 All sharp corners shall be rounded off except the 
dibble point. 

6.2 The dibble handle, dibble point and foot push 
support shall be free from defects such as cracks, rust, 
burrs and other manufacturing defects. 

6.3 The welding whereever done shall not be porous. 

6.4 The steel pipe, if used for handle shall be 
galvanized or painted with rust preventive coating. 

6.5 The dibble point shall be painted with a rust 
preventive coat. 

7 PERFORMANCE TEST 

All the three dibble points shall be tested in different 
forest areas for sowing 10 seeds or planting 10 plants. 
After the test the dibble points shall not show any sign 
of wear or bluntness. 

8 DESIGNATION 

The dibble iron shall be designated by the number of 
this Indian Standard as: 

Dibble Iron, IS 14524. 

9 MARKING AND PACKING 
9.1 Marking 

The dibble iron shall be clearly marked with the 
fallowing information: 



1 



IS 14524 : 1998 



a) Manufacturer' s name or registered trade-mark; 

b) Batch, code or serial number; and 

c) Size. 

9.2 BIS Certification Marking 

Each Dibble iron may also be marked with the 
Standard Mark. 

9.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 



and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the license for the 
use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 

9.3 Packing 

The dibble iron shall be suitably packed as agreed to 
between the purchaser and supplier to avoid damage 
during transport and handling.

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and 
attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

B{S has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publication), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue 
of *BIS Handbook* and "Standards Monthly Additions'.
